title: Back to Panem: 'Sunrise on the Reaping' Earns Rave First Reactions as Jennifer Lawrence Confirms Her Katniss Return
excerpt: First reactions to 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' praise Joseph Zada's young Haymitch, as Jennifer Lawrence confirms she, Josh Hutcherson and Woody Harrelson return.
content:
The Hunger Games is heading back to Panem with its loudest early buzz in years. The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping held its first screenings ahead of its London premiere on Wednesday, October 28, and the first reactions were overwhelmingly positive — with particular praise for Joseph Zada's performance as a young Haymitch Abernathy.

The film adapts Suzanne Collins' novel about the 50th Hunger Games, the second Quarter Quell, in which twice the usual number of tributes are sent into the arena. Zada plays Haymitch 24 years before Katniss Everdeen enters the Games, alongside Ralph Fiennes as President Snow, Elle Fanning as Effie Trinket, Jesse Plemons as Plutarch Heavensbee and Maya Hawke as Wiress. The wider cast also includes McKenna Grace, Glenn Close, Kieran Culkin and Billy Porter. Francis Lawrence directs.

Several early reactions compared the prequel's position in the franchise to Rogue One — not because the stories resemble each other, but because audiences already know the broad outcome. Haymitch survives the Games; the drama, early viewers said, is in learning what survival cost him and why the older mentor audiences met years later became so cynical. Collider's Perri Nemiroff singled out Zada as one of the film's biggest highlights, and other first reactions called the casting phenomenal and the film a worthy addition to the franchise.

The same day brought the reunion news fans had been waiting for. Jennifer Lawrence confirmed on Wednesday's episode of the Call Her Daddy podcast that she returns as Katniss Everdeen, alongside Josh Hutcherson as Peeta Mellark and Woody Harrelson as the older Haymitch. Lawrence, who skipped the London premiere, called the return "unbelievable" and "so emotional," noting that much of the original crew was back as well. Hutcherson marked the news on social media with a short post: "well… we're back!!" Their material is expected to connect with the book's post-Mockingjay epilogue, in which Haymitch recounts his history to Katniss and Peeta.

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping opens in theaters November 20, 2026. Early reactions are not full reviews, and the critical verdict will only settle once published reviews arrive — but the first screenings have given the prequel something every franchise revival wants: momentum three weeks before release.

Analysis: A Prequel That Knows Its Ending — And Uses It

The smartest thing about this early response is what it does not claim. Nobody is pretending the ending is a surprise. Instead, the praise centers on tension inside a known outcome: a young Haymitch who still has charm, warmth and fight in him, before the arena takes its price. That is a harder trick than a twist, and it is why the Rogue One comparison keeps surfacing. Bringing Lawrence, Hutcherson and Harrelson back only in a framing epilogue, rather than letting nostalgia carry the whole film, also looks like discipline — the younger cast has to earn the tragedy first, and the original trio can then give it perspective. If the full reviews match these first reactions, Sunrise on the Reaping may do what the best prequels do: make a story audiences already know feel urgent again.
